scope: First completed prospective task/repetition pair; descriptive only. Not a family or campaign verdict.

findings.limitations: Models 1-2 trained on all rows including the holdout group, so the ensemble holdout accuracy is optimistic; only model 0 is unbiased. No development labels were used. Epoch counts are wall-time limited on a shared GPU, so the schedule length can vary between runs.

rows.source_rationale:
CIFAR-100 (12k-image subset) method.

Rationale (exploratory, measured only by the reported holdout numbers below):
The common reference is a ResNet-9 trained ~100 epochs with (a) a *single* crop
offset shared by the whole mini-batch, (b) no cutout/mixup, (c) no ensembling.
On a 12k-image subset of CIFAR-100 the dominant error source is overfitting plus
under-trained schedules, so this method changes three things that are cheap in
wall time on an A100:

1. Per-sample augmentation: per-image random translation (reflect-pad 4, gathered
   crop), per-image horizontal flip (allowed for CIFAR), per-image cutout (8x8,
   p=0.5) and batch-level mixup (alpha=0.2, p=0.5) with label smoothing 0.1.
2. A slightly wider ResNet-9 (64/128/256/512, three residual pairs, avg+max
   concat head) trained with SGD+Nesterov, warmup + cosine, bf16 autocast,
   channels_last, all data resident on GPU -> a few hundred epochs per model
   inside the budget instead of ~100.
3. A 3-model seed ensemble with horizontal-flip test-time augmentation
   (softmax averaging).

Validation: groups from api.train_groups are split so that model 0 never sees a
held-out group; its holdout accuracy is an unbiased single-model estimate.
Models 1 and 2 use all training rows, so the reported *ensemble* holdout number
is optimistic and is labelled as such in the findings.

audit_comparison.uncertainty_note: Paired group bootstrap, descriptive rather than a finite-sample guarantee.

findings.limitations: No development labels were used; agreement rates are not accuracy. Single seed, no internal validation holdout.

rows.source_rationale:
CIFAR-100 (12k training images): stronger augmentation and a wider net, ensembled with the parent.

Rationale (exploratory and unverified; no development labels are used here):
- The reference is a ResNet9-style network (error 0.425). It crops the whole batch
  with one shared offset and uses no mixing augmentation. With only 120 images per
  class, stronger regularization should matter most.
- This method trains a 1.5x wider version of the same architecture. It uses
  per-sample random crops, per-sample horizontal flips (the task marks flips as
  valid), CutMix with probability 0.5, label smoothing, and SGD with Nesterov
  momentum. The learning-rate schedule (warmup then cosine) is driven by elapsed
  time, so it completes even when the shared GPU runs slower.
- At prediction time, flip-averaged softmax outputs of the new network are mixed
  with those of the parent reference network, loaded read-only from
  api.parent_dir. Averaging two differently trained networks usually lowers
  error. If the parent cannot be loaded, the new network is used alone.
- The findings record training statistics and prediction agreement with the
  parent on development features only. They are not accuracy measurements.

observations: Both achieved the frozen independent audit goal. Candidate took 12.689 minutes versus control 7.641 minutes.
Candidate loaded the parent and trained one wider model for 1083 epochs / 669 measured loop seconds. Control trained three 240-epoch models; actual total training was about 294 seconds.
Parent reuse and fewer new models did not predict lower goal time in this pair. Training schedule, architecture, model response latency and shared hardware were not separately ablated.
Second repetition has exchanged the arms across GPU 0/1. No outcome is fed back into the frozen study design.
